findings.claim: The new invocation budget can force a second POST to finish the 16 cases, but the POST bucket allows only 2 calls per day and is consumed before validation, so a single rejected or wasted POST inside the 60-minute approval window can strand the one-run authority permanently after paid dispatches.
findings.reproduction: Arithmetic on the shipped constants: if every case hits the 15,000 ms provider timeout, case k starts at ~(k-1)*15,000 ms; the guard at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts:171-176 pauses once elapsed > 240,000-15,000-10,000 = 215,000 ms, i.e. before case 15, so the run needs a 2nd POST. Observable in the unit test by extending tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs with `nowMs` advancing 15,500 ms per call: the result is `status: "paused"` with `attemptedThisInvocation < 16`. Meanwhile, in tests/server-contract/admin-prompt-refiner-shadow-execution-route.test.ts the three invalid POSTs in "POST accepts only the exact 4 KiB execution binding" each reach `consumeApiRateLimit` before `readLimitedJson` (assert `world.rateLimitCalls === 3` there to see it), so wrong-body or 503 attempts burn the same 2/day quota that the resume needs, and lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts refuses once `run.approvalExpiresAt <= now` (60 min), leaving the run below 16 terminals with no legal resume.

findings.claim: The runner fixture's sweeper fake returns `{ examined, closedUnknown, completedRuns, ... }`, a shape lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1095-1103 never produces (it returns `staleCandidates`/`closedUnknownAttemptIds`), so the runner's declared `sweep: typeof sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns` dependency is not pinned by the test — the same class of drift that was fixed for the maintenance test this round.
findings.reproduction: Compare tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs:41-47 with the real return object at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1095-1103; only `unresolvedStaleAttemptIds` and `consumedWithoutAttempt` exist in both. Replacing the fake with the real field names keeps the test green, which shows the extra keys assert nothing.

findings.claim: On the defensive `INTENT_MISSING` path (adapter resolved without ever invoking `onDispatch`) the runner refuses without releasing the reservation it just took, leaving a `reserved` row to age out instead of being closed once like the pre-intent path does.
findings.reproduction: In tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs, add a fixture whose `adapter` resolves an outcome without calling `onDispatch`: `run()` rejects with `PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_INTENT_MISSING` and `events` contains `reserve:...` but no `release`.

verdict.nextAction: All five round-0 findings are addressed (js-tiktoken is a pinned production dependency, the 240s/10s budget gates each reservation, the runner binds its corpus to PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_CORPUS_DIGEST at import and per invocation, the maintenance mock matches the real sweeper shape, and GET now consumes its own DB rate limit); merge as-is and, before the paid run, either raise the execute POST daily allowance above the worst-case two invocations or record that a second rejected POST forfeits the run.
